requirement: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.index.chapter`. I did not request implementation source, and I did not reassess the cited `requirements.index.detail_pages` or `requirements.index.chapter.default` beyond how this requirement applies them.

**Directive syntax: standalone, empty body, opening fence of at least three colons, closing fence at least as long.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[marker_accepts_long_fences_and_ignores_examples]` checks these cases:
- A four-colon directive with a four-colon closer is accepted, and the matched range is asserted exactly.
- A five-colon closer on a four-colon opener is accepted.
- A three-colon directive inside a code fence is ignored.
- A directive nested in a `req` example is ignored.
- A directive with no closer is an error.
- A directive with a non-empty body is an error.
- A closer shorter than the opener is an error.
- A two-colon directive is not a directive.
- A directive preceded by inline text is not standalone and is ignored.

**At most one directive per book.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[repeated_index_markers_fail_with_a_clear_error]` covers two directives in different chapters and two in the same chapter. Both cases assert `preprocess_book` returns an error containing "only one". The accepted marker test also shows that a code-fenced or example-nested marker does not count toward that limit.

**Index listing every requirement in rendered chapters, each linking to its detail page.**
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` asserts one table row for each of five requirements. Each row links to `requirements-index/<name>.html`, and the evidence-state column has the expected value for each. It also asserts the table's column alignment.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` covers examples ((example) rows), a requirement in a nested child chapter, and names containing `.md`. It asserts the links from the definitions and the detail-page order.

**Directive replaced by the index table.** The explicit-marker tests assert that `{requirements-index}` no longer appears in the index chapter. The first test above also asserts the table is present. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons]` asserts the explicit chapter keeps its placement: the book still has three items and no extra chapter is appended.

**No directive, so the default chapter is generated.**
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters]` covers a book with no definitions and a book containing only prose with a code-fenced marker. Both get a generated chapter with the expected title, path, number, no source file and an index table.
- `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` covers the default chapter in a book that has definitions.

The finer details of the default chapter belong to `requirements.index.chapter.default`, which has its own tests.

These tests also assert behavior the other tests miss, such as the assertions on the replaced marker. I found no plausible violating behavior that the supplied tests would accept.

text: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.

When a book contains no standalone `{requirements-index}` directive, `habeas mdbook` MUST append a new top-level chapter titled "Requirements index" at `requirements-index.md`, containing the index table, even when the book defines no requirements or examples. The generated chapter MUST have no source file or edit target. Its section number MUST be one greater than the largest numbered top-level chapter, or 1 when no top-level chapter is numbered.
